Prosecution witnesses deposed regarding the offence in the present matter as follows :-
10.PW-1 Siddharth Goyal (complainant) who deposed that on 03.04.2022, he was coming by foot and reached near GK-1, M Block Market and was talking on phone and in the meanwhile two persons came on motorcycle, all on a two wheeler but he did not remember the make of the same,
one person snatched his mobile phone from his hand and ran away thereafter, he shouted for help and chased the accused persons.

Meanwhile, one police official who was on official vehicle, also chased the two wheeler of the accused and after sometime, the two wheeler of the robbers collided with a vehicle of a police official and due to imbalance, both of them fell down.
Meanwhile, both the accused persons were apprehended and thereafter they were identified by the complainant at the police station.
Thereafter, his statement was recorded vide Ex.PW1/A and his phone had fallen down on the spot.

Further, that the witness identified the accused at the police station, however, the witness stated that accused Salman was not the person who had snatched his mobile phone.
The witness did not identify the accused Abdulla @ Shahrukh in the Court.
Thereafter the witness was declared hostile as he did not support the story of prosecution and denied all suggestions.

11.PW-2 HC Jagdish deposed that on 03.04.2022, he was on patrolling duty along-with HC Murari Lal and on that day, when he reached near C-58, GK-I, he found that two persons were driving scooty and one person was chasing them.
Thereafter, they stopped the car in front of the scooty, due to which the scooty fell down on the road.
At that time, Ct. Digvinay also came to the spot on his motorcycle and thereafter they met the complainant Siddharth Goyal who disclosed regarding the incident.

Thereafter, they all along-with both accused persons went to the police station and investigation the present matter was conducted and accused persons were arrested and their personal search were conducted and their disclosure statements were recorded by the IO.
The case property was seized and the sketch memo of the knife was prepared.
IO recorded his statement.
He identified the case property in the court.
12.PW-3 ASI Murari deposed on the lines of PW2 and mentioned regarding the manner in which the investigation was conducted.

remaining witnesses cited by the prosecution were police officials.
They being formal in nature were not examined and prosecution evidence was closed.
14.Matter was fixed for recording of statement of accused U/Sec 313 CrPC and all the incriminating evidence was put to accused persons which they denied.

They claimed that they have been falsely implicated and they were innocent and they had not committed any crime and they had been apprehended falsely in the present matter and nothing was recovered from their possession.
They did not prefer to lead defence evidence.
Consequently, matter was fixed for final arguments.

4 15.Before appreciating the evidence, brought on record by the prosecution, I must mention here the law of appreciating evidence of the witnesses.

Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case titled as Satish Bombaiya Vs. State, 1991 JCC 6147, had observed:
"While appreciating the evidence of a witness, approach must be whether the evidence of the witness read as a whole appears to have a ring of truth.

Once that impression is formed then undoubtedly it is necessary for the court to scrutinize the evidence more particularly keeping in view the deficiencies, drawbacks and infirmities pointed out in the evidence as a whole and evaluate them to find out whether it is against the general tenor of the evidence given by the witness and whether earlier evaluation of evidence is shaken as to render it unworthy of behalf.

Minor discrepancies on trivial matters not touching the core of the case, hyper technical FIR No.91/2022, PS G.K. I State Vs.Abdulla @ Shahrukh & Anr. Page No. 8 of 10 approach by taking sentences torn out of context here and there from the evidence, attaching importance to some technical error committed by the investigating officer not going to the root of the matter, would not ordinarily permit rejection of the evidence as a whole.

entities.text: PS G.K. I State Vs.Abdulla @ Shahrukh & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The main thing to be seen is, whether those inconsistencies go to the root of the matter or pertained to the insignificant aspects thereof.
In the former case, the defence may be justified in seeking advantage of the inconsistencies in the evidence.
In the latter, however no such benefit may be available to it.
That is a salutary method of appreciation of evidence in criminal cases.
16. So, in the wake of above mentioned law, evidence brought on record, has to be read as a whole and has to be appreciated as a whole.
It has to be seen whether shortcomings highlighted by accused, go to the root of the matter and if it so goes, then in that eventuality only evidence has to be discarded.
During course of final arguments accused stated that he has been falsely implicated in the present matter and had not committed the offence.
17.In the present matter, PW1 Siddharth Goyal was the star witness of the prosecution.
Aforesaid witness did not support the story of the prosecution.
He did not depose about involvement of accused persons in any manner, in alleged crime which had taken place with the complaint.
The aforesaid fact or allegation are not made by PW1 during his testimony recorded during trial.
So, he did not support prosecution story despite being cross examined by Ld. Addl. P.P. for the State.
FIR No.91/2022, PS G.K. I State Vs.Abdulla @ Shahrukh & Anr. Page No. 9 of 10

entities.text: PS G.K. I State Vs.Abdulla @ Shahrukh & Anr.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18.Therefore
, I discarded the testimonies of said eye witness/complainant witness being inconsequential and unreliable in nature.
19.Remaining witnesses were formal in nature and were the police officials who had conducted investigation in this case.
There testimony as such was not sufficient to convict accused with the offences, with which they were charged.
Their testimony only talked about the manner in which they had done investigation.
In the light of absence of veracity of testimonies of public witnesses, there testimony became inconsequential.
It did not help the cause of prosecution.

State vs Abdulla @ Sharukh on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182655409/
5
20.Accused persons were able to raise probable defence of themselves being falsely implicated in this case.
21. So, prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
22. Both accused persons namely Abdulla @ Shahrukh and Mohd. Salman stands acquitted for all the offences in this case.
